reason: Full HTML text (main body, appendices A-B, Tables 1-3) available; short demo-style paper with narrow quantitative evidence.

paper.central_claim: AgentFactory preserves successful task solutions as executable Python subagent code (with SKILL.md), refines saved subagents from execution feedback on later similar tasks, and thereby reduces the effort (orchestrator tokens) needed for similar tasks without manual intervention; subagents are portable to other Python-capable agent systems.
paper.title: AgentFactory: A Self-Evolving Framework Through Executable Subagent Accumulation and Reuse

evidence.quote: We propose AgentFactory, a new self-evolution paradigm that preserves successful task solutions as executable subagent code rather than textual experience.
evidence.support_explanation: States the changed non-weight object: stored experience is executable code instead of text.

evidence.quote: Upon successful completion, the Meta-Agent evaluates the subagent and decides which skills to save as reusable skills.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention/admission decision is made by the same LLM Meta-Agent; no replay, held-out or statistical gate is described.

evidence.quote: The modified subagent is tested against the current task to verify the improvement.
evidence.support_explanation: Validation of a modification is on the triggering task only; no regression check on previously solved tasks is described.

evidence.quote: Upon successful completion, results and improved subagents are promoted from the workspace to the persistent skill library.
evidence.support_explanation: Gives the persistence path: isolated workspace, then promotion to library. No versioning/rollback/retirement is described.

evidence.quote: consists of 15 additional tasks with similar structure but different specific requirements, serving as transfer evaluation targets.
evidence.support_explanation: Batch 2 is built to mirror Batch 1 (Appendix B), so reuse is tested on near-variants authored by the same team.

evidence.quote: We report the average output token count of the orchestrating model per task, excluding token consumption within subagent LLM calls.
evidence.support_explanation: Sole quantitative metric is orchestrator output tokens; subagent LLM cost is excluded, so cost may be shifted rather than saved.

evidence.quote: We ensure that all tasks are completed without runtime errors in all experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Task quality is not scored; completion without runtime error is the only success condition mentioned.

evidence.quote: A notable finding is that Opus 4.6 already shows a significant reduction in orchestration tokens during Batch 1 itself under AgentFactory (4324 vs. 8298 for ReAct)
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported Opus result; Batch 1 reduction occurs before any transfer, so it cannot be attributed to retained subagents from other batches.

Table values (Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6): AgentFactory Batch 1 Sonnet 9199 exceeds ReAct Batch 1 Sonnet 6893; Batch 2 values 2971/3862 vs ReAct 7022/7029 and textual-experience 6210/8223. Single run per cell, no variance.

evidence.quote: This shows the agent autonomously detecting limitations and improving error handling through iterative refinement.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-evolve step is supported by one qualitative README-subagent example over three runs; no quantification.

evidence.quote: the agent writes and executes code for each task, and saves the resulting experience as textual summaries
evidence.support_explanation: Textual-experience baseline is described in one sentence; retrieval, store size and prompts are not specified.

evidence.quote: However, these approaches primarily record successful experiences as textual prompts, verbal reflections, or reasoning traces.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: prior self-evolution stores text; claimed to fail at reliable efficient re-execution (asserted, not measured).

evidence.quote: or by saving executable tool-level skills, as demonstrated by Voyager
evidence.support_explanation: The closest executable-skill-library neighbor is named in one clause; no comparison or differentiation is given in text or experiments.

evidence.quote: In Trajectory 3, the workflow migrated to Claude Code—a different agent system—which first learned how to use the saved subagents by reading the SKILL.md documentation.
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-system portability is one anecdote with no metric.

evidence.quote: We consistently use the same LLM backbone for both the MetaAgent and subagents across all experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Same backbone for all arms; two backbones tested (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6).

evidence.quote: Token counts exclude subagent-internal LLM consumption.
evidence.support_explanation: Confirms the cost metric omits the delegated work and creation/modification calls.

gap.author_gap: Self-evolving agents store experience as text, which cannot reliably guarantee efficient re-execution in complex scenarios.
gap.checked_gap: A real design axis (text vs executable store), but the claim that text fails is asserted and only indirectly tested via an under-specified textual baseline; no dedicated test of executable vs text reliability.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Reflexion/Self-Refine (text reflection), Voyager (executable skill library; named only), AlphaEvolve and Darwin Goedel Machine (code evolution for specialized problems). Voyager-style executable skill accumulation is the closest neighbor and is neither differentiated nor compared against.
gap.residue: No evidence yet on correctness of reused subagents, admission quality, or library degradation over many tasks.
gap.stakes: Re-derivation cost on recurring procedural tasks.
gap.method_response: Store solutions as code with docs and refine on failure; deploy to other agent frameworks.
gap.remaining_gap: Quality-controlled admission, regression-safe modification, true held-out transfer, and total cost accounting remain open.
unresolved: Whether code store beats a well-built text/skill store on correctness (not only orchestrator tokens)

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 15 authored near-variant tasks, an LLM orchestrator that reuses its own saved Python subagents emits fewer orchestrator output tokens than ReAct and a textual-memory agent; subagent-internal cost and output correctness are not measured.
assessment.note: Author-reported results only; nothing was run by us. Central claim 'increasingly robust and efficient as more tasks are encountered' is retained as stated; supported conclusion is narrower.

G.reason: Real design axis (text vs code store) with named prior work, but the failure of text experience is asserted and the closest neighbor (Voyager) is not differentiated.

M.reason: Concrete mechanism (decompose, create, save, modify, deploy) addresses re-execution cost; assumptions about LLM-judged admission and why code beats text are not tested and no distinguishing prediction vs Voyager is given.

X.reason: Operation chain and interfaces are reconstructible, with workspace isolation and promotion; retention gate is Meta-Agent judgement, and versioning, rollback, regression checks and staleness are not described.

E.measurement.reason: Only metric is orchestrator output tokens excluding subagent LLM calls; success is 'no runtime error'; a cost-shifting explanation is unaddressed.

E.causality.reason: ReAct and textual baselines exist, but no store-off on identical tasks, no ablation of modify/tool-allocation, textual baseline under-specified, and Sonnet Batch 1 contradicts the within-batch claim.

E.holdout.reason: Build set (Batch 1) and eval set (Batch 2) are separate, with no leakage evident, but Batch 2 was authored as mirrored variants, so transfer is narrow; cross-system claim is an anecdote.

E.statistics.reason: Sample size (15 tasks) and a negative cell are shown, but there are no seeds, intervals or tests (A2 ladder level 1).

E.cost.reason: Cost is the headline but excludes subagent calls and creation/modification effort; no latency or budget parity beyond same backbone.

rationale: Demo-style system paper: executable subagent library with feedback-driven modify. Only evidence is orchestrator-token savings on 15 mirrored tasks; cost shifting, no ablation, no variance, and no Voyager comparison limit it to a scoped task-level claim.
